early_traditions.label: Earlier traditions
early_traditions.description: Earlier urban and building traditions remain visible through inherited patterns and later reinterpretations.
early_traditions.designIdea: Ask how land, settlement, local materials and inherited forms shape a place.
early_traditions.canadianContext: Colonial ports, settlements and surveys overlay longstanding Indigenous lands and planning systems.
early_traditions.internationalContext: International examples retain their own histories; this period is not a universal stage of progress.

industrial_streetcar.label: Industrial and streetcar city
industrial_streetcar.description: Railways, industry, main streets and expanding urban neighbourhoods reshape many cities.
industrial_streetcar.designIdea: Compare the block, street, workplace and daily trip rather than only the facade.
industrial_streetcar.canadianContext: Canadian rail and port cities grew with shops, workplaces and varied housing; development also involved exclusion and dispossession.
industrial_streetcar.internationalContext: Paris boulevards, iron-and-glass markets and other international references offer comparisons.

reform_interwar.label: Reform and interwar city
reform_interwar.description: Housing reform, garden suburbs, civic improvement and new architectural movements overlap.
reform_interwar.designIdea: Connect design proposals with health, housing, public space and who benefits.
reform_interwar.canadianContext: Adams garden suburbs and the 1919 planning institute sit alongside early 20th-century housing and commercial growth.
reform_interwar.internationalContext: Garden City, Arts and Crafts, Bauhaus and De Stijl have different origins and aims.

postwar.label: Postwar expansion
postwar.description: Rapid housing growth, road building, new suburbs and large institutional projects transform Canadian cities.
postwar.designIdea: Compare access, housing production, open space and the consequences of redevelopment.
postwar.canadianContext: CMHC plan books, Don Mills and urban-renewal debates provide contrasting Canadian cases.
postwar.internationalContext: International modernism and neighbourhood-unit ideas were adapted to different settings.

late_twentieth.label: Late 20th-century change
late_twentieth.description: Conservation, community action, urban regeneration, new housing approaches and renewed transit planning overlap.
late_twentieth.designIdea: Ask how a project changes inherited neighbourhoods and whose choices it expands.
late_twentieth.canadianContext: Rehabilitation, mixed-income neighbourhoods and Vancouver tower-and-podium development are useful comparisons.
late_twentieth.internationalContext: Postmodernism, New Urbanism and other international influences enter different local debates.

contemporary.label: Contemporary city
contemporary.description: Housing intensification, climate response, mobility and public-space redesign shape current planning debates.
contemporary.designIdea: Consider housing choice, daily access, environmental processes and distribution of benefits.
contemporary.canadianContext: Missing-middle reforms, the CMHC catalogue and Vancouver 2026 ODP are current examples; Indigenous-led planning continues.
contemporary.internationalContext: Canadian cities exchange ideas about complete neighbourhoods, transit, public space and adaptation internationally.

context_dependent.label: Era not specified
context_dependent.description: This component or long-running tradition does not establish one design era from the available evidence.
context_dependent.designIdea: Use its placement, connections and documented reference to investigate its history.
context_dependent.canadianContext: A path, court, industrial enclosure or generic planted space can serve many kinds of Canadian neighbourhood.
context_dependent.internationalContext: A regional tradition can continue across periods; functional equipment alone does not date a design.

new_urbanism.label: New Urbanism
new_urbanism.description: Compact, connected neighbourhoods combining different uses and housing choices.
new_urbanism.designIdea: Walkable daily life and well-defined shared public space.
new_urbanism.componentLimit: A compatible frontage or street is one component; a whole-plan assessment is needed.

tod.label: Transit-oriented development
tod.description: Integrating land use with walking, cycling and useful public transport.
tod.designIdea: Access to activities with less dependence on cars.
tod.componentLimit: A station or tall building alone does not establish TOD, service quality or equitable outcomes.

compact.label: Compact infill
compact.description: Adding development within an existing built-up area; form and scale can vary.
compact.designIdea: Use serviced land carefully while considering existing residents and housing choices.
compact.componentLimit: Building form does not prove affordability, tenure or absence of displacement.

place.label: Public-life / placemaking principles
place.description: Organising places around activities and the needs of the people who use them.
place.designIdea: Comfort, sociability and meaningful local use.
place.componentLimit: Benches and attractive paving do not establish a community-led placemaking process.

heritage.label: Heritage continuity / adaptive reuse
heritage.description: Retaining or adapting inherited buildings and urban patterns.
heritage.designIdea: Continuity, cultural identity and reuse of existing fabric.
heritage.componentLimit: A newly generated historic-looking model does not prove a real conservation project.

ecology.label: Green infrastructure
ecology.description: Treating water, habitat, planting and built development as related systems.
ecology.designIdea: Resilience and care for environmental processes.
ecology.componentLimit: Model appearance cannot establish stormwater capacity, biodiversity or carbon performance.

garden_city.label: Garden City / garden-suburb connections
garden_city.description: Combining settlement, landscape, local work and long-term community stewardship.
garden_city.designIdea: Healthy living and shared community benefit.
garden_city.componentLimit: Green space alone is not Garden City planning; land, governance, jobs and housing matter.

city_beautiful.label: Civic composition / City Beautiful
city_beautiful.description: Coordinating civic buildings, axes and public spaces into a formal composition.
city_beautiful.designIdea: Civic identity and a prominent public realm.
city_beautiful.componentLimit: A single Classical building or symmetrical garden is insufficient evidence.

vancouverism.label: Vancouverism
vancouverism.description: Slender towers combined with lower urban edges, public space and an emphasis on sustainable movement.
vancouverism.designIdea: Density with attention to light, views and street life.
vancouverism.componentLimit: The tower-and-podium model alone cannot establish public benefits or the neighbourhood framework.

haussmann.label: Haussmannian urbanism
haussmann.description: Metropolitan restructuring through boulevards, infrastructure and coordinated urban frontage.
haussmann.designIdea: Connectivity and a deliberate city image.
haussmann.componentLimit: A boulevard replica is an illustration of this tradition, not a reproduction of its social history.

complete.label: Complete Streets
complete.description: Allocating street space for safe access by people using different modes and with different abilities.
complete.designIdea: Inclusive mobility and context-sensitive street design.
complete.componentLimit: A section alone does not verify crossings, speeds, networks or accessibility compliance.

shared.label: Shared-street / woonerf principles
shared.description: Low-speed shared space that places pedestrian use and social activity at the centre.
shared.componentLimit: Shared appearance without speed management and accessible navigation is insufficient.

active.label: Walking / cycling network priority
active.description: Providing connected, useful routes for walking and cycling.
active.designIdea: Direct everyday access and alternatives to driving.
active.componentLimit: A disconnected fragment does not establish a usable network.

child.label: Child-friendly / school-street principles
child.description: Designing daily routes and outdoor spaces around children’s access, play and comfort.
child.componentLimit: Safety and accessibility need detailed design and operational checks.

auto.label: Car-oriented layouts / road hierarchy
auto.description: Organising frontage, access or movement around motor vehicles and a hierarchy of roads.
auto.componentLimit: This describes a spatial priority, not the political beliefs of designers or users.

modernist_plan.label: Modernist planning
modernist_plan.description: A comparison lens for freestanding slabs, separated circulation and large-scale composition.
modernist_plan.designIdea: Discuss functional organisation and the relationship of buildings to open space.
modernist_plan.componentLimit: Architectural Modernism and Modernist planning are different; a slab alone proves neither master-plan intent nor historical authorship.

biophilic.label: Biophilic design principles
biophilic.description: Strengthening people’s experience of nature through the built environment.
biophilic.componentLimit: Visible greenery is an opportunity to discuss the principle, not proof of health or environmental outcomes.

landscape.label: Landscape-led / naturalistic public realm
landscape.description: Composing routes, views and activities around landscape character.
landscape.designIdea: Restoration, outdoor experience and attention to the site.
landscape.componentLimit: A park does not establish a complete landscape-urbanism philosophy or an Olmsted attribution.

missing_middle.label: Missing-middle housing
missing_middle.description: House-scale multi-unit homes and clusters, including duplexes, fourplexes, townhouses and cottage courts.
missing_middle.designIdea: Expand housing choice at a modest building scale.
missing_middle.componentLimit: Form alone does not establish affordability, tenure or zoning eligibility. A detached house alone is not multi-unit housing.

historic_urbanism.label: Historic main-street / streetcar urbanism
historic_urbanism.description: Fine-grained blocks, street-facing entrances, local shops and housing form an inherited urban pattern.
historic_urbanism.designIdea: Explore relationships between daily trips, frontages and the street network.
historic_urbanism.componentLimit: A historic-looking street does not document its actual age, former transit service or social history.

complete_neighbourhoods.label: Complete neighbourhoods
complete_neighbourhoods.description: Connect diverse homes with everyday shops, services, parks and community facilities.
complete_neighbourhoods.designIdea: Make daily needs accessible to different residents.
complete_neighbourhoods.componentLimit: One facility cannot establish access, service capacity or equitable outcomes across a neighbourhood.

indigenous_planning.label: Indigenous planning and self-determination
indigenous_planning.description: Planning grounded in Indigenous authority, knowledge, relationships and community priorities.
indigenous_planning.designIdea: Learn whose land and governance shape the city and how Indigenous-led planning continues.
indigenous_planning.componentLimit: This is not an aesthetic. No existing model receives this label from timber, landscaping or cultural-looking motifs.

nonmarket_housing.label: Social, non-profit and co-operative housing
nonmarket_housing.description: Housing organised through public, non-profit or co-operative institutions and tenure arrangements.
nonmarket_housing.designIdea: Compare who owns, manages, funds and can access housing.
nonmarket_housing.componentLimit: Ownership, tenure, rent and affordability cannot be established by the appearance or name of a model.

housing_delivery.label: Standardized small-house delivery
housing_delivery.description: Pattern-book plans and coordinated housing programmes connect individual dwelling design with the supply of homes.
housing_delivery.designIdea: Compare the design of a home with how many homes and their neighbourhoods are delivered.
housing_delivery.componentLimit: An isolated model does not establish a government programme, present affordability, ownership or a street pattern.

contemporary_gabled.label: Contemporary gabled
contemporary_gabled.description: Simple pitched-roof volumes with restrained detailing and contemporary openings or cladding.
contemporary_gabled.designIdea: Use a familiar house silhouette in a current design.

contextual_brick.label: Contextual brick contemporary
contextual_brick.description: Contemporary homes using brick, entrance rhythms and proportions that respond to an existing streetscape.
contextual_brick.designIdea: Add housing while relating to the surrounding urban fabric.
